lines: Opening film: Vesak morning, the estate
By then, I had learnt to hide what my hands did in temples... but I never stopped going.
Opening film: the corridor of shops
There was an amulet shop I often visited. The owner knew me well.
Opening film: the shop's glass door
Every Buddha Day, he held a small chanting for his regular customers. That morning, I went to pay my respects.
Seconds after play begins: the owner looks up from his counter
[warmly] Ah, you came! Happy Buddha Day! Come in, come in. Look around first, ah.
Play: looking at the wall of framed amulets
[quietly] Somdej, Phra Rod, Nang Phaya... every one of them with its own story.
Play: looking at the LP Tim's case behind the counter
LP Tim Khun Paen... he never lets anyone hold that one.
Play: looking at the shop's altar
Lotus, candles, fruit... he must have been preparing since morning.
Play: looking at the photographs of the old masters
The old masters... watching over the whole shop.
Play: the owner calls him over to the counter
Eh, come, come. I got something for you.
Play: at the counter, taking the LP Tim out of its case
Today is Buddha Day, very auspicious. This one, LP Tim Khun Paen, from Wat Lahanrai. I kept it for you very long already.
Play: handing him the LP Tim
[kindly] Wear it. Keep it close to you. It will protect you.
Play: once he wears the LP Tim
[touched] Thank you, Uncle... it feels heavier than it looks.
Play: once he wears it, the chanting about to start
Good, good. Now come, the chanting is starting.
Play: the owner leads the chant, three times
[chanting slowly, reverently] Namo tassa bhagavato arahato samma-sambuddhassa. Namo tassa bhagavato arahato samma-sambuddhassa. Namo tassa bhagavato arahato samma-sambuddhassa.
Play: his hands part from the prayer on their own
[frightened whisper] No... not here. Not in front of everyone...
Play: he rises, and cannot stop it
[shaken] I couldn't stop it... my body was not mine any more.
The trance: the owner sees him dancing
[alarmed] Eh! Eh, boy! You okay or not?!
The trance: the staff man grabs his arms
The trance: the staff man cannot hold him
The trance: the shop girl, frightened
The trance: an auntie praying fast
[praying quickly, under her breath] Amituofo... amituofo... amituofo...
The trance: the owner, quietly, as they give up
[quietly, in awe] Let him... don't touch him. Let him finish.
The trance ends: on his knees, breathing
After the trance: kneeling beside him
[concerned] You know what you were doing just now?
[shaken, out of breath] I knew... I knew everything. I just... couldn't stop.
After the trance: the shop girl
[uneasy] Was he in a trance or what?
[worried] Possessed, maybe... something not clean following him.
After the trance: the owner urges him
[firmly] Tonight, you go and see a medium. I know one, a good one. Go tonight. Don't wait.
Over the black, arriving at the medium's shrine
Play: arriving at the medium's shrine
[uneasy] The last time I stood in front of a medium... I was just a boy.
Play: the medium's assistant, after the incense
You, wait there first. Sifu still seeing people.
Play: the first consultation, a woman
[worried] Sifu, my husband cannot sleep. Every night, he says something is sitting on his chest.
[flatly, certain] Your house... the main door is facing the wrong way. Something followed your husband home.
Burn this. Put the ash in water. Drink it, three days.
Play: the second consultation, a father with his son
[tired, worried] Sifu, my son keeps crying every night. Cannot stop.
[flatly] Your son got a fright. Something saw him at the void deck.
Play: the medium sends them off
Play: his legs carry him to the medium on their own
[frightened] No... not again. My legs were walking on their own.
[flatly, without hesitation] It is a ghost possessing you.
Play: after the roar, the medium's incantation
[shouting, commanding] 天灵灵，地灵灵！太上老君急急如律令！
Play: after the roar, the assistant
[alarmed] Wah! Everybody, step back! Step back!
Scene A: he accepts the reading
Come back seven nights. Bring the things on this list.
[weary] I did everything he told me... and it didn't stop.
Scene B: he tells the medium he is wrong
[firm] You're wrong. It's not a ghost.
Scene B: the assistant throws him out
[shouting] Go! Get out! Don't come back here!
Scene B: out on the street
[shaken] I answered his certainty with my own... and whatever it was, it heard me.
Scenes C and D: he thanks the medium
[tired] I thanked him, and told myself it was over. I didn't want to think about it any more.
[thoughtful] A ghost, he said... Maybe. Maybe not. I couldn't prove it either way.
Scene D: looking up at the night
[resolved, quietly] If I wanted the truth... I would have to go and find it myself.
The closing narration in all four outcomes
[reflective] After that night, I started visiting other shops... other masters... looking for answers.
Over the black at the end of all four outcomes
And some of the pieces I found... answered back.
I took his word, and did everything he said.
I told him he was wrong.
I thanked him, and tried to forget it.
I thanked him, and kept looking for the truth.
